place.source_title: Engels & Krudwig Wine Company building, Sandusky (1863)

brief: A lake-shore winery: a long two-storey building of rough grey limestone blocks with arched cellar doors, a stepped gable, small windows and a timber sign, beside a second stone wine hall. Two photos. Older than 1970: Lake Erie island wineries (Heineman's, Lonz) are 19th-century stone cellars; no newer example. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: the Engels & Krudwig Wine Company (Sandusky OH, 1863): a three-storey building of rock-faced limestone blocks with arched wooden doors, wine cellars beneath, a carved 'THE WINERY' sign and a wooden entry hood; a brick addition

why.note: Lake Erie's island wine industry: stone winery buildings with vaulted cellars
